transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I can’t shake this feeling that I’ve failed my family and that everything that’s gone wrong is my fault. My wife and my cousin got really worried about me and insisted that I come in to talk to someone. I just feel like I've let everyone down.
Have you ever had a similar period of feeling depressed or hopeless before, or is this the first time it has happened? Also, did this start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

No, I've never felt this hopeless before; this is the first time, and it started about eight months ago. It all began after a terrible argument with my adult daughter about my long work hours, which led to her moving out of state and cutting off almost all contact with me.
Since this started, have you also had other depressive symptoms like poor sleep, low energy, loss of interest, poor appetite, or trouble concentrating most days?

Yes, I lie awake for hours staring at the ceiling and wake up around three in the morning with my mind racing, which leaves me completely worn out. I've also lost interest in things I used to love, like grilling for the family or closing deals at work, because it all just feels pointless now. I'm not really sure about my appetite or concentration, though.
Have these symptoms been present most days for the entire 8 months, or did they improve at any point after the conflict with your daughter?

No, they haven't gotten any better at all. It has been completely steady and constant every single day for the entire eight months since my daughter moved away. There hasn't been any break or relief; it has just felt like a continuous, heavy cloud hanging over me.
Have these symptoms been affecting your ability to function at work or at home, and have you had other symptoms like changes in appetite, concentration, or thoughts that life is not worth living?

Yes, my work numbers have dropped so much that my manager has pulled me aside twice, and at home I've let bills pile up and completely withdrawn from my family. I haven't really noticed changes in my appetite or concentration, but I do constantly feel like everyone would be better off if I weren't around. It's gotten to the point where I catch myself wishing I wouldn't wake up, or even picturing driving off the highway when I'm alone in my car.
Have you had any actual thoughts of killing yourself, or made any plan or taken any steps to harm yourself?

Yes, I've had those thoughts, especially when I'm driving alone on the highway and picture just steering off the road. But I haven't made an actual, concrete plan or taken any steps to hurt myself yet. I just feel so much guilt and honestly believe my family would be better off without me.
Did your symptoms begin within a few months of your daughter moving away, and have they felt directly tied to that event? Or do they seem out of proportion to the stressor or unrelated to it?

Yes, they started right after that horrible fight and her moving away eight months ago. It feels completely tied to that, because the guilt of driving my own daughter away and failing her as a father has consumed me ever since.
Have you ever had any periods before this where you felt depressed or lost interest in things for at least two weeks, even if there was no major stressor?

No, I have never experienced feelings like this before this whole situation with my daughter started eight months ago. Before that, I was always motivated, focused on my work, and loved being with my family.
Have you had any period of feeling completely back to normal since this started, or has the low mood and loss of interest been present nearly every day for the entire 8 months?

No, I haven't had any periods of feeling back to normal at all. It has been a continuous, heavy weight on me every single day for the entire eight months since my daughter moved away. The low mood and loss of interest have just been constant without any breaks.
Did these symptoms start within a few months of the conflict with your daughter and feel directly tied to that event, or did they continue for a long time even after the stressor was over?

They started right after our big fight and her moving away eight months ago. The stress isn't actually over because we still haven't reconciled and barely speak, so these feelings have been constant ever since.
Have the symptoms felt mainly like a reaction to the conflict with your daughter and the ongoing family strain, or have they seemed to continue even when you are not thinking about that situation?

While the fight and her moving away definitely started all of this, the heavy feeling has become a constant presence that just doesn't lift. Even when I'm doing other things, like trying to work or holding my grandson on FaceTime, the dark cloud is still there. It persists even when I'm not actively thinking about the conflict.
Have you had any periods of at least two weeks during these eight months when your mood and interest returned to normal, or has the depression been present nearly every day the whole time?

No, I haven't had any breaks like that at all. The heavy mood and lack of interest have been there nearly every single day since my daughter left. It's just been one long, continuous struggle without any relief.

Did the depression start within about 3 months of your daughter moving away, and does it feel mainly tied to that stressor? Or has it lasted longer than expected or felt out of proportion to the situation?

Yes, it started right around the time my daughter moved away eight months ago and has been constant ever since. While it is definitely tied to that painful event, the feelings of guilt, failure, and emptiness have lasted for so long and grown so intense that they now feel completely overwhelming and out of proportion, taking over every part of my life.

Before this started, had you ever gone through a period of at least two weeks with similar depression or loss of interest when there was no major stressor? Or has this been a new reaction that began after your daughter moved away?

No, I have never experienced anything like this in my entire life before now. This is a completely new reaction for me that started about eight months ago, right after my daughter moved away following our terrible argument. I was always a motivated, happy family man before all of this happened.
Have you had any periods of at least two weeks during these eight months when your mood and interest returned to normal, or has the depression been present nearly every day the whole time?

No, there haven't been any times where my mood or interest returned to normal, not even for a few days. It has been constant and present nearly every single day for the entire eight months since my daughter moved away. There has been absolutely no break from this heavy feeling.

Have you had any periods during these eight months when you felt back to your usual self for at least a few days or weeks, or has the low mood and loss of interest been present nearly every day the whole time?

No, I haven't felt like my usual self even for a single day. It has been a steady, continuous weight since my daughter moved away eight months ago, and I just haven't had any relief from this low mood. It's been present nearly every single day without any breaks.
Do you feel your sadness and guilt are mainly a normal reaction to this family conflict, or do they feel much more intense than you would expect from that stressor?

It feels far more intense and consuming than a normal reaction. The guilt is completely paralyzing, and I feel like I've ruined my daughter's life and don't deserve forgiveness. This constant dark cloud feels much deeper and more permanent than just being upset over an argument.

Did your symptoms start within about 3 months of the conflict with your daughter, and do they feel clearly tied to that stressor? Or did they continue for longer than expected or seem out of proportion to what happened?

Yes, they started almost immediately after our big fight and her moving away about eight months ago, and it has been a steady, continuous struggle ever since. While others might think I should have moved past it by now, the pain and guilt feel completely tied to that event. It has only grown heavier and more overwhelming over time.
Have you ever had any time during these 8 months when the sadness and loss of interest were much better for at least a couple of weeks, or has it been nearly constant the whole time?

No, there hasn't been any time like that at all. The sadness and loss of interest have been completely constant and steady over the entire eight months without any real breaks or periods of improvement. I haven't had even a couple of weeks where I felt significantly better or regained my interest in things; it has just been a continuous, heavy cloud since my daughter moved away.
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself on purpose, or do you feel you might act on the thoughts of driving off the road?

I do have those thoughts when I'm driving alone, picturing driving off the road because I feel like my family would be better off financially and emotionally without me. But actually acting on it scares me, and I feel a lot of hesitation about doing it. I haven't taken any steps or made any real plans to go through with it.
Did these symptoms start within 3 months of the stressful event, and do they seem mainly tied to that event? Or did they begin later or feel unrelated to it?

Yes, they started almost immediately, within days of our big fight and her moving away eight months ago. These feelings are deeply tied to that event and the painful realization of how badly I fractured my relationship with her. It has all stemmed directly from that moment.
Did your symptoms begin within about 3 months of the stressful event, and do they feel mainly tied to that event? Or did they start later or seem unrelated to it?

Yes, they started right after our big fight and my daughter moving away eight months ago. My struggles are directly tied to that painful event, as everything began spiraling from that exact point. It really feels like that was the moment everything fell apart.
Have you ever had any period of at least two months since this started when you felt back to your usual self, or has the low mood and loss of interest been present nearly every day the whole time?

No, I haven't had any breaks or felt like my usual self at all since this started. It has just been a steady, heavy feeling nearly every single day for the entire eight months since my daughter moved away. It never seems to lift, not even for a little while.

Before this started, were you able to cope with stress and daily life pretty well, and do you feel this reaction is much more intense than what most people would have after the same event? Or has the low mood and loss of interest felt more like a depression that came on without being tied to the stressor?

Before this, I coped very well with life and took a lot of pride in my busy sales job and hosting our family gatherings. This heavy mood and loss of interest are definitely tied to the fight with my daughter and her moving away, rather than coming out of nowhere. It has just hit me incredibly hard, far beyond any normal stress I've ever had to deal with.
Have you had any period of at least two months since this started when you felt back to your usual self, or has the low mood and loss of interest been present nearly every day the whole time?

No, I haven't had any breaks or felt back to my usual self at all. It has been a steady, continuous struggle every single day for the entire eight months since my daughter moved away. This heavy feeling just never lifts.
Did your symptoms start within 3 months of the stressful event, and do they seem clearly tied to it? Or have they lasted much longer than expected or felt out of proportion to the stressor?

Yes, they started immediately after our fight and her moving away eight months ago, so it was definitely within that time. It has been going on steadily ever since and has completely taken over my life. It feels far more intense and heavy than just a normal reaction to a family disagreement.
Did your symptoms start within 3 months of the fight with your daughter, and have they felt clearly tied to that stressor? Or did they begin later or seem unrelated to it?

Yes, they started pretty much right after the big fight and my daughter moving away, which was about eight months ago. It feels completely tied to that event, as I haven't been the same since she left and my mind constantly replays that argument.
Have your symptoms been present for more than 6 months after the stressful event, or did they start within 3 months and then gradually improve?

Yes, my symptoms have been present for the entire eight months since my daughter moved away, starting right after our fight. They haven't gradually improved at all; in fact, they have remained heavy and constant this whole time.
Have you had any periods of at least two months during these eight months when you felt back to your usual self, or has the low mood and loss of interest been present nearly every day the whole time?

No, I haven't had any periods of feeling back to my usual self at all. The low mood and loss of interest have been steady and present nearly every day for the entire eight months. There hasn't been any break or relief from this heavy feeling.

Before this started, had you ever had a period of at least two weeks with the same kind of depression or loss of interest when nothing stressful was happening, or is this the first time it has ever occurred?
No, this is the very first time I have ever experienced these feelings. I have never gone through anything like this before in my life.
